items.title: Von Freeman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: One day, he and I were drinking together at the Pershing... Ben was sitting there. I’m so in awe of the man... He says, “It’s about that time.” I said, “For what?” He said, “We need another one, don’t we?”

ctx.x: This World War II thing, did it just so happen that this recording ban happened around the same time as that?

Yeah. When you couldn’t record? That caused a lot of stuff to go down. That when singers came to the fore, because back when I was a kid, we’d go see the big bands. They’d always have some singers that would sit on the side. They might sing two numbers a night. One. Nobody cared, because we’re all there to see Pres and all the cats in Duke’s band. We’d see Ben Webster. Lunceford’s band, we went to hear certain cats. All the bands we had certain cats that we all wanted to hear, and the ladies wanted to hear them…
Who were the top cats in Lunceford’s band? Just as an aside.
